question.:question/problem: Find the general solution to the differential equation $f'(x)=3 e^{- 2 x}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, notice that the derivative term is already isolated on the left:

$$
\begin{aligned}f'(x) &=3 e^{- 2 x}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate both sides of the equation with respect to $x,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int f\prime(x)\,\text{d}x &=\int (3 e^{- 2 x})\,\text{d}x \\ f(x) &=\int (3 e^{- 2 x})\,\text{d}x \\ &=1\cdot \left(- \frac{3 e^{- 2 x}}{2}\right)+C \\ &=- \frac{3 e^{- 2 x}}{2}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

recipe_operations: multiply instead of divide by power/inner factor
omit last primitive or omit outer coefficient

Then, we integrate both sides of the equation with respect to $x,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int f\prime(x)\,\text{d}x &=\int (- \frac{3 \sin{\left(3 x \right)}}{2}- e^{- 4 x}- 2 x)\,\text{d}x \\ f(x) &=\frac{1}{2}\cdot \int (- 3 \sin{\left(3 x \right)})\,\text{d}x+\frac{1}{2}\cdot \int (- 2 e^{- 4 x})\,\text{d}x+\frac{1}{2}\cdot \int (- 4 x)\,\text{d}x \\ &=\frac{1}{2}\cdot \left(\cos{\left(3 x \right)}\right)+\frac{1}{2}\cdot \left(\frac{e^{- 4 x}}{2}\right)+\frac{1}{2}\cdot \left(- 2 x^{2}\right)+C \\ &=\frac{\cos{\left(3 x \right)}}{2}+\frac{e^{- 4 x}}{4}- x^{2}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

knowledge_point.title: Finding the General Solution of a Differential Equation Using Integration

question.:question/problem: Find the general solution to the differential equation $-4f'(x)=\frac{6}{x - 3}- 3 e^{- 2 x}+6 x.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we rearrange the equation to isolate the derivative term:

$$
\begin{aligned}f'(x) &=- \frac{3}{2 \left(x - 3\right)}+\frac{3 e^{- 2 x}}{4}- \frac{3 x}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate both sides of the equation with respect to $x,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int f\prime(x)\,\text{d}x &=\int (- \frac{3}{2 \left(x - 3\right)}+\frac{3 e^{- 2 x}}{4}- \frac{3 x}{2})\,\text{d}x \\ f(x) &=- \frac{1}{4}\cdot \int (\frac{6}{x - 3})\,\text{d}x- \frac{1}{4}\cdot \int (- 3 e^{- 2 x})\,\text{d}x- \frac{1}{4}\cdot \int (6 x)\,\text{d}x \\ &=- \frac{1}{4}\cdot \left(6 \ln{\left(\left|{x - 3}\right| \right)}\right)- \frac{1}{4}\cdot \left(\frac{3 e^{- 2 x}}{2}\right)- \frac{1}{4}\cdot \left(3 x^{2}\right)+C \\ &=- \frac{3 \ln{\left(\left|{x - 3}\right| \right)}}{2}- \frac{3 e^{- 2 x}}{8}- \frac{3 x^{2}}{4}+C.\end{aligned}
$$
